questions.question: Which invention patented by Henry Ford in 1911 was used in the Model T and other automobiles?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: "In 1911, he was awarded a patent for the transmission mechanism that would be used in the Ford Model T and other automobiles."
Incorrect. The article does not mention a patent for a four-cylinder engine block; it specifically references the transmission mechanism.
Incorrect. While the Model T had a left-hand steering wheel, the article attributes the patent to the transmission mechanism, not the steering wheel.
Incorrect. The moving assembly belt was introduced later for production; the article mentions it was introduced in 1913, not patented in 1911.

questions.question: What was the name of the first self-propelled automobile completed by Henry Ford in 1896?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: "These experiments culminated in 1896 with the completion of a self-propelled automobile, which he named the Ford Quadricycle."

Incorrect. The franchise system was established earlier to support dealerships, not the 1913 production boost.

questions.question: What was the price of a basic Model T touring car in 1916?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: "By 1916, as the price dropped to $360 for the basic touring car, sales reached 472,000."
Incorrect. $825 was the 1908 price; by 1916 the price had dropped to $360.
Incorrect. The price was well below $1,000 by 1916.
Incorrect. The Model T never reached $2,000; it was consistently affordable.

questions.question: Which newspaper owned by Henry Ford promoted his antisemitic views in the 1920s?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: "In the 1920s, Ford promoted antisemitism through his newspaper *The Dearborn Independent*..."
Incorrect. The Detroit Free Press was not owned by Ford.
Incorrect. The New York Times was not his publication.
Incorrect. The Chicago Tribune was not his newspaper.

questions.question: What was the primary reason Henry Ford gave for painting all Model Ts black?
options: quicker drying time of the paint
customer demand for a single color
answer_explanations: Correct. The article notes: "Until the development of the assembly line, which mandated black because of its quicker drying time, Model Ts were available in other colors..." and later quotes Ford: "Any customer can have a car painted any color that he wants so long as it is black."
Incorrect. While cost is a factor, the article specifically cites quicker drying time due to the assembly line.
Incorrect. The article does not mention customer demand as the reason.
Incorrect. The article does not state aesthetic preference.

questions.question: Which company did Henry Ford acquire in 1922?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says: "In 1922, Ford also purchased Lincoln Motor Co."
Incorrect. Cadillac was founded earlier and was not acquired by Ford in 1922.
Incorrect. General Motors was a competitor, not acquired by Ford.

questions.question: Who became the president of Ford Motor Company in December 1918?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: "Henry Ford turned the presidency of Ford Motor Company over to his son Edsel Ford in December 1918."
Incorrect. Henry Ford II took over much later, in 1945.
Incorrect. C. Harold Wills was an engineer, not president.
Incorrect. Barney Oldfield was a race driver.

questions.question: What was the name of the partnership formed between Henry Ford and Alexander Y. Malcomson to manufacture automobiles?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article mentions: "They formed a partnership, Ford & Malcomson, Limited, to manufacture automobiles."
Incorrect. The Detroit Automobile Company was a separate earlier venture.
Incorrect. The Henry Ford Company was formed later after the partnership dissolved.
Incorrect. Ford Motor Company was incorporated later, after the partnership.
